title: Interfacial chirality-induced magnetic-field-free switching with high energy efficiency in all-vdW heterostructures
authors: Kai-Xuan Zhang, Suik Cheon, Seungbok Lee, Joonyoung Choi, Jihoon Keum, Hyuncheol Kim, Yeochan An, Woonghee Cho, Suhan Son, Jingyuan Cui, Pyeongjae Park, Younjung Jo, Jun Sung Kim, Hyun-Woo Lee, Je-Geun Park
abstract: Chirality, a central concept across many scientific disciplines, continues to inspire the discovery of novel physical phenomena. In condensed matter physics, structural chirality - defined by the absence of mirror plane symmetries - has primarily been explored in bulk materials. However, new chiral phenomena can emerge uniquely at the interface, distinct from their bulk counterparts, when a chiral material forms a heterostructure. Here, we demonstrate that all van-der-Waals (vdW) heterostructure composed of the chiral Co1/3TaS2 and the achiral vdW ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 exhibits two distinct and unconventional spin-orbit torques originating from the interfacial chirality. These torques enable magnetic-field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization with ultralow current density ~ 10^6 A/cm^2 and minimal power dissipation < 10^15 W/m^3. Moreover, by replacing Fe3GeTe2 with a similar vdW ferromagnet, Fe3GaTe2, but of higher Curie temperature, we achieved the magnetic-field-free switching at room temperature in the Fe3GaTe2/Co1/3TaS2 vdW heterostructure. Our findings establish interfacial chirality as a powerful new handle for spintronic control, opening a new pathway to explore chirality-induced phenomena beyond the bulk symmetry constraints - and paving the way toward highly efficient, low-power spintronic devices based on all-vdW heterostructures.
summary: This work demonstrates a new pathway for ultra-low power magnetic switching by utilizing interfacial chirality in vdW heterostructures. By generating two unconventional spin-orbit torques, the system achieves field-free magnetization reversal with minimal energy loss. This establishes interfacial chirality as a powerful design handle for next-generation spintronic devices.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate highly energy-efficient, magnetic-field-free switching of perpendicular magnetization using interfacial chirality effects in all van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures.
main_result: Magnetic-field-free switching was achieved with ultralow current densities ($\sim 10^6 	ext{ A/cm}^2$) by exploiting two unconventional spin-orbit torques originating from the interface's chirality. Replacing one material allowed this effect to persist up to room temperature.
method: The study combines experimental transport measurements (measuring $R_{xy}$ vs. writing current) with detailed symmetry analysis of the resulting spin-orbit torque terms.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an all vdW heterostructure, specifically $	ext{Fe}_3	ext{GeTe}_2/	ext{Co}_{1/3}	ext{TaS}_2$. The key physics relies on the structural chirality at the interface, which generates unique torques beyond what bulk symmetry predicts.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall resistance ($R_{xy}$), critical switching current density ($J_{sw}$), and power dissipation ($ rac{J_{sw}^2}{\sigma}$).
important_parameters: Ultralow current densities ($\sim 10^6 	ext{ A/cm}^2$) and minimal power dissipation ($< 10^{15} 	ext{ W/m}^3$); switching observed across a temperature range including room temperature with material substitution.
main_assumptions: The observed phenomena are uniquely attributed to the breaking of mirror plane symmetries (interfacial chirality) leading to unconventional spin-orbit torques.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device structure, temperature dependence of resistance kinks and anomalous Hall effect, and crucially, hysteresis loops showing magnetization switching occurring solely under an applied current with zero external magnetic field. The symmetry analysis details the three-fold dependence of the torque on writing current direction.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system (vdW heterostructure), theoretically derives unconventional spin-orbit torques based on interfacial chirality, and then presents experimental evidence showing robust, low-power magnetic-field-free switching across various temperatures and material variations.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics rather than fundamental quantum dynamics, the concept of using symmetry breaking (chirality) to engineer novel, highly controllable quantum phenomena at interfaces is relevant to understanding emergent behavior in complex quantum systems.
